claims.text: Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based alloys can have a mixed martensitic or multiphase structure.
The mixed or multiphase structure in conventionally processed MnNiSi-based alloys gives rise to a pronounced magnetocaloric effect.
Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based alloys have limited mechanical toughness and ductility.
Hot deformation under an approximately 0.5 T magnetic field will promote a uniform twin-martensite structure in MnNiSi-based alloys.
Processing near or above the martensitic-start temperature permits the thermoplastic deformation needed for the proposed microstructural change.
A suitable deformation rate can promote twin formation during hot magnetic processing.
An approximately 0.5 T field promotes atomic diffusion during severe hot deformation.
The proposed treatment will refine the martensitic microstructure and make its twins more uniform.
The proposed treatment will reduce defect concentrations.
The proposed treatment will improve grain-boundary integrity.
The applied magnetic field enhances atomic mobility and rearranges martensitic variants into a more homogeneous twin structure.
A homogeneous twin structure reduces stress concentrations and crack-initiation sites.
Reducing stress concentrations and crack-initiation sites increases mechanical strength and ductility.
The magnetostructural transition remains essentially intact after hot deformation under an approximately 0.5 T field.
The magnetically processed MnNiSi-based alloy will have higher strength and ductility than an otherwise similarly processed no-field baseline.
The magnetically processed alloy will retain entropy change and Curie temperature similar to the no-field baseline.
Fields substantially below 0.5 T may be insufficient to produce a uniform twin-martensite structure.
Fields substantially above the proposed moderate range may destabilize the magnetostructural transition and reduce magnetocaloric performance.
